plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value of $20 maximizes my expected profit—bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth, and bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. There's no benefit to shading my bid in this format, so truthful bidding is optimal.

Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) when I win, bidding exactly my value of $29 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than to others, and I never overpay since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not mine. In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids, and you pay only the second-highest bid, never overpaying. Shading down doesn't help since payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (unless you're bidding to influence winning probability). With value $45, I'll bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit without risk of overpaying.
